newsitem.title: USA: DMG ups Lucent EPS view, others may follow.
newsitem.headline: DMG ups Lucent EPS view, others may follow.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc's solid revenue growth and sustained profit margins during a seasonally weak March quarter led at least one Wall Street analyst to boost earnings estimates on the company.

Jim Parmalee, telecom equipment analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said he boosted his earnings estimates for Lucent's fiscal 1997 and 1998 years in light of the strong results it reported for its second quarter ended in March.
His earnings projection for the fiscal year ending September 1997 was now $2.20 per share from $2.15 and for fiscal 1998 it was $2.60 per share from $2.50 previously.
J.P Morgan analyst Neil Danzger said he also is weighing boosting his estimates on Lucent, marking the second time in the past few weeks he has lifted the projections.
Danzger had previously raised his fiscal 1997 estimate to $2.15 from $2.10 and his 1998 estimate to $2.50 per share.
"I may nudge them up further following this announcement," he said following the Lucent earnings report Thursday.

"Lucent posted strong results especially in a seasonally weak quarter," DMG's Parmelee said. "I was most impressed by the breadth across the three main business units and the international growth, which was above our expectations.

Lucent reported double-digit revenue growth in each of its three main product units -- network systems, business commmunications and microelectronics. However, revenues for its much smaller consumer products fell 41 percent.
The company posted a profit of $0.10 per share in the March quarter versus a loss of $0.16 per share in the year ago period.
"The results were good," Danzger agreed, pointing especially to progress Lucent demonstrated during the quarter in expense control and holding the line on gross margins.
